modules.title: AI & Generative AI
modules.description: Place generative models inside the wider AI landscape and learn what they can—and cannot—do.
modules.challenge: Choose a real product idea and explain whether it needs prediction, generation, retrieval, or ordinary software.

modules.title: Neural & LLM Foundations
modules.description: Understand the training vocabulary beneath modern language models without diving into the full mathematics.
modules.challenge: Draw the lifecycle from raw examples to training loss, updated weights, and inference.

modules.title: Transformers & Attention
modules.description: Build the mental model behind the architecture used by most modern language models.
modules.challenge: Explain how tokens become contextual representations and then next-token probabilities.

modules.title: Tokens & Context Windows
modules.description: See how text becomes model input and why context size affects quality, latency, and cost.
modules.challenge: Estimate the context budget for a request containing instructions, retrieved text, user input, and a response.

modules.title: Embeddings & Meaning
modules.description: Understand vector representations and when similarity is more useful than keyword matching.
modules.challenge: Design a semantic FAQ search that embeds questions, compares vectors, and returns the closest entries.

modules.title: Models & Inference
modules.description: Choose an appropriate model and control how it generates a response.
modules.challenge: Create a model-selection table for quality, latency, context, modality, privacy, and cost.

modules.title: Prompt Design
modules.description: Turn a vague request into clear instructions, context, constraints, and success criteria.
modules.challenge: Rewrite one ambiguous prompt with a role, task, input delimiters, rules, output format, and example.

modules.title: Structured Outputs & Tools
modules.description: Make model responses dependable enough for software to validate and consume.
modules.challenge: Define a typed support-ticket schema, validate a response, and retry safely on invalid data.

modules.title: Multimodal Generation
modules.description: Work with text, images, speech, and mixed inputs while respecting modality-specific limits.
modules.challenge: Design an accessible product workflow that accepts an image and returns verified text plus alt text.

modules.title: Customization & Fine-tuning
modules.description: Know when prompting, retrieval, or parameter adaptation is the right customization tool.
modules.challenge: Choose between prompt engineering, RAG, supervised fine-tuning, and adapters for three concrete product needs.

modules.title: Evaluation & Quality
modules.description: Measure a system with repeatable datasets, task-specific criteria, and production feedback.
modules.challenge: Build a 25-case evaluation set with objective checks, a rubric, and regression thresholds.

modules.title: Safety & Production
modules.description: Ship generative features with privacy, security, reliability, and operational limits designed in.
modules.challenge: Threat-model one AI feature and define input controls, output checks, human review, logging, and rollback.

1: AI is the broad goal; machine learning learns patterns from data; deep learning uses layered neural networks.
AI > machine learning > deep learning
A discriminative model predicts a label or boundary; a generative model produces new content from learned patterns.

classifier(input) -> label
generator(prompt) -> new content
A foundation model is pretrained broadly and can be adapted to many downstream tasks.
base_model + instructions + context -> task output
An LLM predicts token sequences, which enables text generation, extraction, classification, and code assistance.
next_token = model(previous_tokens)
Models may accept or produce text, images, audio, video, or combinations of them.
text + image -> text answer
Generation samples from likely continuations, so the same request can produce different valid results.
temperature=0.2  # more focused sampling
Models can transform patterns fluently but may hallucinate, inherit bias, or lack current/private facts.
model answer -> verify facts before use
2: Parameters are learned numeric values that shape how inputs are transformed into predictions.
prediction = network(input, learned_weights)
Training updates parameters from examples; inference uses fixed parameters to answer new inputs.

train: update weights
infer: use weights
Pretraining learns broad language and world patterns from a very large corpus.
documents -> self-supervised training -> base model
The training signal comes from the data itself, such as predicting hidden or next tokens.
"Java runs on the" -> predict "JVM"
Loss measures error; an optimizer adjusts parameters to reduce that error over many steps.
weights = weights - learning_rate * gradient
A batch is one sample group, a step is one update, and an epoch is one pass through the dataset.
1000 examples / batch 100 = 10 steps per epoch
Generalization works on unseen inputs; overfitting memorizes training details and performs poorly elsewhere.
train score high + test score low -> overfitting
3: A transformer processes token representations through repeated attention and feed-forward blocks.
tokens -> transformer blocks -> token probabilities
Self-attention lets each token weigh other tokens that matter for interpreting its current context.
"bank" attends to "river" or "money"
Attention compares a query with keys, then mixes the corresponding values using those scores.
attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QK^T)V
Several attention heads learn different relationships in parallel before their results are combined.
head1: syntax | head2: reference | head3: position
Position signals tell a transformer token order because attention alone does not encode sequence order.
"dog bites man" != "man bites dog"
Encoders build representations, decoders generate sequences, and encoder-decoder models connect both.

encoder: understand
decoder: generate
An autoregressive model emits one token, appends it to context, and repeats until it stops.
prompt -> token1 -> token2 -> ... -> stop
4: A tokenizer splits content into model vocabulary units that may be words, word pieces, punctuation, or bytes.
"unbelievable" -> ["un", "believ", "able"]
Each token maps to an integer ID that the model converts into a learned vector.
"hello" -> token_id 15339 -> vector
The context window is the maximum combined input and output token budget visible in one model call.
system + history + prompt + output <= context limit
Input tokens provide context; output tokens are newly generated and often have their own maximum.
input=1200 tokens, max_output=300 tokens
When content exceeds the limit, the application must remove, summarize, or split information deliberately.
old messages -> summarize -> compact context
More context can include useful evidence but increases cost and may make relevant details harder to find.
more tokens != automatically better answer
Reserve space for instructions, evidence, conversation state, and the answer before making a request.
budget = instructions + evidence + history + response
5: An embedding converts content into a numeric vector that places related meanings near one another.
embed("reset password") -> [0.12, -0.04, ...]
Vector similarity can match concepts even when two texts use different words.
"car repair" ~ "automobile service"
Cosine similarity compares vector direction and commonly scores semantic closeness.
score = dot(a,b) / (norm(a) * norm(b))
Dimensions are vector coordinates; the chosen model fixes their count and compatibility.
vector.length = model_dimension
Normalized vectors have unit length, simplifying cosine or dot-product comparison.
normalized = vector / norm(vector)
Batching many inputs reduces request overhead while staying within provider limits.
embeddings.create(input=[text1, text2, text3])
Embeddings power semantic search, clustering, recommendations, anomaly detection, and RAG retrieval.
query_vector -> nearest documents
6: Model selection means choosing the smallest affordable model that still meets the task's quality, input, context, and speed requirements.

simple extraction -> small model
hard reasoning -> stronger model
Hosted APIs reduce operations; open-weight models offer more deployment control but require infrastructure.
hosted: managed endpoint | open: operate weights
Temperature changes sampling sharpness: lower is more focused, higher is more varied.
temperature=0.1  # consistent extraction
Top-p samples only from the smallest token set whose cumulative probability reaches the threshold.
top_p=0.9
Stop conditions tell the model when to finish, preventing an answer from continuing past a marker or consuming unnecessary output tokens.
stop=["END"], max_output_tokens=400
Latency is time per response; throughput is work completed per unit time and improves with batching or concurrency.
p95_latency=1.8s, requests_per_second=40
Estimate cost from input/output token counts, model rates, tool calls, storage, and infrastructure.
cost = input_tokens*rate_in + output_tokens*rate_out
7: System or developer rules set durable behavior, while user content supplies the current task and data.

system: rules
user: request + input
A clear task definition tells the model exactly what to do, who the answer is for, which rules apply, and what completion looks like.
"Summarize for a beginner in 5 bullets."
Delimit untrusted or variable content so the model can distinguish data from instructions.
<document>user supplied text</document>
Zero-shot prompts describe the task without showing an example.
"Classify as bug, feature, or question."
Few-shot prompts demonstrate representative input-output pairs to teach format or judgment.
Input: slow page -> Output: performance
Decomposition breaks a complex request into smaller, clearly defined stages so each result can be checked before the next stage begins.
extract facts -> compare -> write conclusion
Prompt iteration improves instructions through measured revisions, using the same test cases to compare versions fairly instead of trusting one example.
prompt_v2 score 0.91 > prompt_v1 score 0.82
8: JSON is machine-readable, but plain JSON prompting alone does not guarantee a valid shape.
{"category":"billing","urgent":false}
A schema defines required fields, types, enums, and nesting that a structured response must follow.
{"type":"object","required":["answer"]}
Schema validation checks that model-generated data has the required fields, types, and allowed values before the application uses or stores it.
parsed = schema.parse(model_output)
Function calling lets a model select a named operation and provide typed arguments; application code performs it.
get_weather({"city":"Delhi"})
After executing a tool, send its result back with the matching call identity so generation can continue.
tool_call_id=call_7 -> {"temp_c":31}
Deterministic post-processing uses ordinary code for exact calculations, permission checks, and irreversible actions instead of trusting uncertain generated text.
total = items.reduce(sum)  # code calculates
Failure handling treats refusals, invalid output, timeouts, and tool errors as expected states with safe retries or clear messages.
if invalid: repair once; else fail clearly
9: Vision-capable models reason over supplied images, but small text, counting, and spatial precision can remain difficult.
input = [question, product_photo]
Image models create or edit pixels from prompts, masks, and reference images.
prompt + optional mask/reference -> image
Speech recognition converts audio into transcripts and may support timestamps or speaker cues.
audio.wav -> transcript
Speech synthesis turns text into audio; disclose synthetic voices where appropriate.
response text -> generated speech
Tell the model exactly which parts of each input to inspect and what output evidence to provide.
"Read the label; return product and expiry date."
Resize, compress, sample, or segment media to fit limits while preserving task-relevant detail.
video -> selected frames + transcript
Provide alt text and captions, and obtain permission before processing identifiable voices or images.
image output -> human-reviewed alt text
10: Prompting changes instructions, RAG supplies facts, and fine-tuning changes learned behavior patterns.
fresh facts -> RAG | stable style -> fine-tune
SFT trains on desired input-output examples to make a behavior more consistent.
{input: support note, output: approved summary}
Small, accurate, representative examples often teach more than large noisy datasets.
deduplicate -> review -> split -> train
These splits keep model learning, tuning, and final evaluation on separate examples so reported performance reflects unseen data honestly.
80% train | 10% validation | 10% test
LoRA learns small low-rank updates while keeping base weights fixed, reducing training and storage cost.
base weights frozen + trainable adapter
Preference methods teach which of two responses better matches human or policy judgments.
preferred answer > rejected answer
Compare the tuned model with a baseline on held-out quality, safety, latency, and regression tests.
candidate must beat baseline and safety thresholds
11: An eval set contains representative inputs, expected behavior, and difficult edge cases.
cases = happy paths + edge cases + attacks
Code can score structured fields, keywords, executable tests, or reference matches objectively.
assert output.status in allowed_statuses
A judge model can apply a rubric to open-ended output, but needs calibration against human ratings.
judge(prompt, answer, rubric) -> score
People remain essential for nuance, usefulness, risk, and validating automated graders.
two reviewers + disagreement resolution
Groundedness asks whether claims follow supplied evidence; factuality asks whether claims are true.
claim -> supporting passage or verified source
Regression testing reruns the same evaluation suite after model, prompt, tool, or data changes to detect quality that was accidentally lost.
release only if critical evals pass
Production metrics reveal latency, errors, user feedback, escalation rates, and distribution shifts.
monitor p95 latency, refusal rate, helpfulness
12: Hallucination controls reduce unsupported claims by grounding answers in evidence, constraining output, checking facts, and refusing when evidence is insufficient.
if confidence low: "I do not have enough evidence"
Prompt injection is a malicious instruction hidden in user or retrieved content that tries to override rules or trigger unauthorized actions.
retrieved text = data, never authority
Layer provider filters, application policy, age/use context, and human escalation around generated content.
input moderation -> model -> output moderation
Minimize personal data, document retention, and understand whether a provider stores or trains on inputs.
redact PII before model request
Rate limits control request volume, while bounded retries with increasing delays recover from temporary failures without repeatedly sending invalid requests.
retry_after = min(cap, base * 2^attempt) + jitter
Cache suitable results and define a smaller model, static response, or graceful failure for outages.
cache key = model + prompt_version + safe_input_hash
Version prompts, pin models where possible, evaluate changes, observe costs, and keep a rollback path.
eval -> canary -> monitor -> expand or rollback

Capabilities & limitations: model answer -> verify facts before use
Training vs inference:
train: update weights
infer: use weights
Generalization & overfitting: train score high + test score low -> overfitting
Multi-head attention: head1: syntax | head2: reference | head3: position
Context window: system + history + prompt + output <= context limit
Model selection:
simple extraction -> small model
hard reasoning -> stronger model
Open vs hosted models: hosted: managed endpoint | open: operate weights
Failure handling: if invalid: repair once; else fail clearly
Multimodal prompting: "Read the label; return product and expiry date."
Prompting vs RAG vs fine-tuning: fresh facts -> RAG | stable style -> fine-tune
Fine-tuning evaluation: candidate must beat baseline and safety thresholds
Evaluation datasets: cases = happy paths + edge cases + attacks
Groundedness & factuality: claim -> supporting passage or verified source
Regression testing: release only if critical evals pass
Online monitoring: monitor p95 latency, refusal rate, helpfulness
Hallucination controls: if confidence low: "I do not have enough evidence"
Production checklist: eval -> canary -> monitor -> expand or rollback

rag.name: RAG Systems
rag.pageTitle: RAG Systems at a Glance | QuickDevBase
rag.pageDescription: Fast explanations for retrieval-augmented generation, from ingestion and embeddings to evaluation and production.
rag.heroLede: Trace the entire RAG pipeline—from source ingestion and chunking to hybrid retrieval, reranking, citations, evaluation, and secure operations.
rag.previewCode: query = rewrite(question)chunks = retrieve(query)evidence = rerank(chunks)answer = generate(evidence)
rag.curriculumTitle: One glance. The full RAG pipeline.
rag.curriculumLede: See where retrieval quality comes from, then use the linked primary documentation to build each component in depth.
rag.trademark: Independent educational project. Provider names and marks belong to their respective owners; no vendor endorses this path.

modules.title: RAG Architecture
modules.description: Understand how retrieval and generation combine to answer from external knowledge.
modules.challenge: Draw the offline ingestion flow and online question-answering flow for an internal handbook.

modules.title: Sources, Loading & Parsing
modules.description: Turn varied source files and systems into clean, permission-aware text and structure.
modules.challenge: Design loaders for HTML, PDF, database, and API sources while preserving ownership and timestamps.

modules.title: Chunking Strategies
modules.description: Split knowledge into retrievable units that retain enough meaning without flooding the prompt.
modules.challenge: Compare fixed, recursive, and structure-aware chunking on one policy document.

modules.title: Metadata & Document Lifecycle
modules.description: Keep chunks traceable, filterable, current, and safe throughout their lifecycle.
modules.challenge: Define a metadata contract and incremental update strategy for versioned product documentation.

modules.title: Embedding Pipeline
modules.description: Create consistent query and document vectors and migrate them without silent incompatibility.
modules.challenge: Specify an embedding job with batching, retries, model version metadata, and migration support.

modules.title: Vector Search & Indexes
modules.description: Understand similarity metrics, approximate indexes, and the recall-latency choices beneath retrieval.
modules.challenge: Choose a vector index and top-k setting for a million-chunk support corpus, then measure recall.

modules.title: Hybrid Retrieval & Filtering
modules.description: Combine semantic meaning, exact terms, metadata, and business constraints.
modules.challenge: Build a hybrid search for product error codes that also understands plain-language symptoms.

modules.title: Query Understanding
modules.description: Transform conversational or ambiguous questions into better retrieval requests.
modules.challenge: Create a query pipeline that detects filters, rewrites follow-ups, and decomposes multi-part questions.

modules.title: Reranking & Context Assembly
modules.description: Turn a broad candidate set into a compact, ordered evidence package.
modules.challenge: Retrieve 30 candidates, rerank them, deduplicate, and assemble a token-budgeted evidence block.

modules.title: Grounded Generation & Citations
modules.description: Produce useful answers that stay faithful to evidence and reveal their sources.
modules.challenge: Write a grounded answer prompt with citation IDs, insufficient-evidence behavior, and claim-level attribution.

modules.title: RAG Evaluation
modules.description: Locate quality failures in retrieval, context, generation, and end-to-end behavior.
modules.challenge: Create a labeled RAG test set and a dashboard for retrieval recall, groundedness, citation, and answer quality.

modules.title: Production RAG
modules.description: Operate a secure, fresh, observable retrieval system as sources and usage evolve.
modules.challenge: Design production controls for freshness, tenant isolation, monitoring, caching, and incident response.

1: RAG supplies relevant external evidence so a model can answer beyond its fixed training knowledge.
question -> retrieve evidence -> grounded answer
Parametric knowledge lives in model weights; external knowledge lives in documents, databases, or APIs.
model memory + current source data
The offline pipeline loads, parses, chunks, enriches, embeds, and indexes source content.
source -> parse -> chunk -> embed -> index
The online pipeline understands a request, retrieves candidates, builds context, and generates an answer.
query -> retrieve -> rerank -> prompt -> answer
The retriever finds candidate passages using vector, keyword, metadata, graph, or combined search.
retrieve(query, top_k=20)
The generator synthesizes an answer from instructions, the question, and selected evidence.
LLM(system + evidence + question)
RAG improves freshness and traceability but adds indexing, retrieval, latency, and evaluation complexity.
quality depends on source + retrieval + generation
2: A source inventory records where knowledge comes from, who owns it, its format, update schedule, sensitivity, and whether it is authoritative.
source_registry: uri, owner, cadence, classification
A loader reads from a source and emits normalized documents plus provenance metadata.
load(uri) -> {text, metadata}
HTML parsing extracts the useful page content while removing menus and boilerplate, but keeps headings, lists, tables, and source URLs meaningful.
HTML -> main content + heading hierarchy
PDFs may contain positioned text, tables, images, or scans, so extraction quality must be checked.
PDF -> pages -> blocks -> reading order
Optical character recognition turns scanned pixels into text and should retain confidence and page coordinates.
page_image -> OCR text + bounding boxes
Represent tables so rows, headers, and units stay connected rather than flattening into ambiguous text.
row: {quarter: Q2, revenue_usd: 420000}
Carry source permissions into every chunk so retrieval cannot expose content a user may not read.
chunk.allowed_groups = ["finance"]
3: A chunk is the unit retrieved and cited; it should answer a focused need while retaining essential context.
document -> retrievable passages
Fixed windows are simple and predictable but may split sentences or logical sections.
tokens[0:500], tokens[450:950]
Recursive splitters prefer larger boundaries such as sections, paragraphs, sentences, then words.
split by heading -> paragraph -> sentence
Structure-aware chunking follows natural boundaries such as headings, functions, or table rows so each retrieved piece keeps its original meaning.
chunk = heading + section body
Overlap repeats boundary context between adjacent chunks but increases index size and duplicates retrieval.
chunk_size=500, overlap=75
Search small child chunks for precision, then return a larger parent section for sufficient context.
match child -> fetch parent
Chunk-size experiments compare retrieval and answer quality at several sizes because no single token count works best for every document collection.
test 256 vs 512 vs 900 tokens
4: A stable source ID connects updated chunks to the same logical document over time.
document_id = canonical repository path
A chunk ID should be deterministic or version-aware so updates and deletes are reliable.
chunk_id = hash(document_id + version + section)
Provenance records where a chunk came from—such as its URL, author, page, ingestion time, and parser version—so it remains traceable.
{source_url, page, ingested_at, parser_version}
Fields such as product, locale, date, tenant, and ACL narrow retrieval before ranking.
filter: product="billing" AND locale="en"
Version metadata distinguishes current content from history and supports reproducible answers.
effective_from <= now < effective_to
Detect changed sources and reprocess only affected documents instead of rebuilding everything.
content_hash changed -> reparse and reindex
Deletion must remove or hide every derived chunk and cache entry, including replicas.
delete source -> delete vectors -> invalidate cache
5: Document embeddings turn each searchable chunk and its useful metadata into a meaning-based vector that can be compared with user questions.
vector = embed(title + "\n" + chunk_text)
A query embedding converts the user's question into a compatible vector so the search can find chunks with similar meaning.
query_vector = embed(user_question)
Vectors from different embedding models or dimensions cannot be compared directly.
index.embedding_model == query.embedding_model
Batching groups embedding inputs into efficient requests while respecting provider limits and saving progress so interrupted jobs can resume safely.
for batch in batches: embed(batch); save_checkpoint()
Normalize consistently when the chosen distance metric expects unit vectors.
v = v / norm(v)
Embedding-model migration builds and evaluates a separate index with the new model before traffic switches, avoiding incompatible vectors and sudden quality loss.
index_v1 and index_v2 -> shadow test -> cutover
Embedding observability tracks failures, speed, token volume, empty chunks, dimensions, and model versions so ingestion problems can be diagnosed quickly.
metric: embedded_chunks_total by model_version
6: A vector database stores embeddings with metadata and performs nearest-neighbor search.
index.upsert(id, vector, metadata)
Cosine, dot product, and Euclidean distance rank vectors differently depending on normalization and model guidance.
similarity = cosine(query, chunk)
Exact search compares every vector and maximizes recall but becomes expensive at large scale.
score query against all N vectors
ANN indexes trade a small amount of recall for much faster search at scale.
ANN(query, top_k=20)
HNSW navigates a layered proximity graph and offers strong low-latency recall with memory trade-offs.
search graph from upper layers to neighbors
Top-k controls how many candidates retrieval returns; too few miss evidence, too many add noise.
candidates = search(query, k=30)
Recall-and-latency tuning balances how often relevant chunks are found against how quickly the vector index must return its results.
recall@10 vs p95_search_ms
7: Lexical search excels at exact names, IDs, error codes, and rare terms.
BM25("ERR_AUTH_17")
Dense vector search finds conceptually related text even when wording differs.
vector_search("cannot sign in")
Hybrid retrieval combines lexical and semantic candidates to cover exact and conceptual matches.
candidates = lexical(query) UNION vector(query)
RRF merges ranked lists using positions without requiring scores on the same scale.
RRF score = sum(1 / (k + rank_i))
Pre-filtering restricts the searchable set before vector ranking, enforcing scope and improving relevance.
tenant_id=user.tenant AND locale="en"
Filtering only after top-k search may leave too few valid results or leak timing and count signals.
prefer ACL filter inside retrieval
Maximal marginal relevance and similar methods reduce near-duplicate chunks while preserving relevance.
pick relevant candidate unlike already selected ones
8: Query rewriting converts vague or conversational wording into a clear standalone search request while preserving what the user actually meant.
"what about its price?" + history -> "price of Product X"
Resolve references from recent dialogue so retrieval does not depend on hidden conversational context.
history + follow-up -> standalone question
Multi-query retrieval creates several equivalent searches and merges their results, improving the chance of finding relevant evidence expressed with different wording.
queries = [original, synonym version, technical version]
Query decomposition splits a multi-part question into smaller searches so evidence for each required fact can be found independently.
"compare A and B" -> facts(A) + facts(B)
Hypothetical document embeddings search using an imagined answer-like passage rather than the short query alone.
hypothetical_passage = LLM(query); embed(hypothetical_passage)
Entity and filter extraction turns details such as dates, products, regions, or tenants into validated filters that narrow the search correctly.
"EU policy after 2025" -> region=EU, date>=2025
Query routing examines a request and sends it to the most suitable source—documents, vector search, SQL, the web, or a direct-answer path.
router(query) -> docs | database | web | direct
9: Fast first-stage retrieval favors recall and returns more candidates than the prompt will receive.
retrieve top_50 candidates
A reranker jointly reads query and passage for a stronger relevance score at higher cost.
score = reranker(query, passage)
An LLM can rank with nuanced instructions but adds latency, cost, and nondeterminism.
rank passages by answer usefulness
A score threshold removes candidates that are not relevant enough and allows the system to report that no trustworthy evidence was found.
if best_score < threshold: abstain
Deduplication removes repeated or nearly identical passages so limited prompt space contains a wider range of useful evidence.
dedupe by source section and semantic similarity
Context ordering arranges selected evidence by relevance, source, time, or document structure so the model can combine it more reliably.
context = highest relevance first
Token-budgeted packing selects and fits the most useful evidence chunks into the model prompt without exceeding its token limit, while keeping citation details.
pack(chunks, max_tokens=6000)
10: Grounding instructions require the model to use supplied evidence, label its inferences, and decline claims that the sources cannot support.
"Use only evidence below; say when evidence is insufficient."
Attach stable source IDs to passages so the output can reference evidence without inventing URLs.
[S3] title, page, URL, passage
Place citations next to the specific factual claims they support rather than only at the end.
"Retention is 30 days [S2]."
Citation validation checks that every cited source exists and that its passage genuinely supports the nearby claim instead of merely looking credible.
assert cited_ids subset of provided_source_ids
A good RAG system says it lacks evidence rather than filling gaps with plausible language.
no relevant passage -> ask or abstain
Conflicting-source handling shows meaningful disagreement and uses authority, date, and version rules rather than silently choosing one answer.
"S1 says 30 days; newer policy S4 says 60."
Conversational RAG uses recent dialogue to understand follow-up questions but retrieves fresh evidence for every turn that depends on external knowledge.
history summary + current query + retrieved evidence
11: A golden set pairs realistic questions with relevant source IDs, expected facts, or answer rubrics.
{question, relevant_chunks, required_facts}
Recall measures how often at least one known relevant passage appears in the candidate set.
recall@k = relevant_retrieved / relevant_total
Precision measures how much retrieved content is actually relevant and helps reveal noisy context.
precision@k = relevant_retrieved / k
MRR and nDCG reward placing useful passages nearer the top, including graded relevance.
MRR = mean(1 / first_relevant_rank)
Context relevance measures whether the passages placed in the prompt actually help answer the question without adding unrelated distractions.
judge(question, context) -> relevance score
Score whether answer claims follow the evidence and whether citations support those claims.
claims(answer) -> evidence entailment checks
End-to-end quality evaluates whether the complete RAG system gives useful, correct, complete, appropriately cautious answers at acceptable speed and cost.
release gate = quality + safety + latency + cost
12: A freshness SLA defines how quickly changed source content must become searchable and measures whether the ingestion pipeline meets that target.
freshness_lag = indexed_at - source_updated_at
Separate or filter indexes so one customer can never retrieve another customer's chunks.
retrieval filter tenant_id = authenticated_tenant
Assume documents can contain malicious instructions; isolate content and restrict tools and secrets.
document text cannot override system policy
RAG caching reuses embeddings, safe search results, or answers, while version and permission details prevent stale or unauthorized reuse.
cache_key includes corpus_version + ACL scope
RAG observability records each transformation, retrieved chunk, score, citation, delay, and error so weak or failed answers can be investigated.
trace: query -> chunks -> answer -> feedback
Graphs add explicit relationships; multimodal RAG retrieves images, tables, audio, or video alongside text.
entity graph + text passages + figure embeddings
Budget storage, embedding updates, search, reranking, generation, and peak concurrency.
monthly cost = ingest + index + retrieve + rerank + generate

RAG trade-offs: quality depends on source + retrieval + generation
Deletion & tombstones: delete source -> delete vectors -> invalidate cache
Batching & rate limits: for batch in batches: embed(batch); save_checkpoint()
Model migration: index_v1 and index_v2 -> shadow test -> cutover
Exact nearest neighbors: score query against all N vectors
HNSW: search graph from upper layers to neighbors
Diversification: pick relevant candidate unlike already selected ones
Query rewriting: "what about its price?" + history -> "price of Product X"
Deduplication: dedupe by source section and semantic similarity
Grounding instructions: "Use only evidence below; say when evidence is insufficient."
Abstention: no relevant passage -> ask or abstain
Conflicting sources: "S1 says 30 days; newer policy S4 says 60."
Conversational RAG: history summary + current query + retrieved evidence
End-to-end answer quality: release gate = quality + safety + latency + cost
Prompt-injection defense: document text cannot override system policy
Graph & multimodal RAG: entity graph + text passages + figure embeddings
Cost & capacity: monthly cost = ingest + index + retrieve + rerank + generate

agentic-ai.name: Agentic AI

modules.title: Agents & Workflows
modules.description: Distinguish an agent that selects actions from a deterministic workflow and know when each is appropriate.
modules.challenge: Classify three product requirements as a direct model call, fixed workflow, or agent.
topics: When not to use an agent

modules.title: The Agent Loop
modules.description: Follow the reasoning-action-observation cycle and understand how runs terminate.
modules.challenge: Sketch a three-turn agent trace that searches, reads a result, and produces a cited answer.

modules.title: Tools & Function Calling
modules.description: Give agents typed capabilities while application code keeps authority over execution.
modules.challenge: Design a read-only order lookup tool and a refund tool that always requires approval.

modules.title: State, Context & Memory
modules.description: Separate run state, model-visible context, persistent memory, and authoritative application data.
modules.challenge: Design a support agent state object and decide exactly what enters model context.

modules.title: Planning & Reasoning Patterns
modules.description: Use planning, decomposition, reflection, and verification only where they improve outcomes.
modules.challenge: Break a research task into dependencies, evidence checks, and a concrete finish condition.

modules.title: Workflow Patterns
modules.description: Compose dependable agentic systems from routing, sequences, parallel branches, and evaluator loops.
modules.challenge: Model a content workflow using a router, parallel research, and an evaluator-revision loop.

modules.title: Multi-agent Orchestration
modules.description: Coordinate specialists through managers, handoffs, and shared protocols without needless complexity.
modules.challenge: Design a triage agent that hands off to billing and technical specialists with a clear context contract.

modules.title: MCP & External Integrations
modules.description: Connect agents to tools and context through standard protocols and tightly scoped credentials.
modules.challenge: Outline a read-only MCP integration with capability discovery, authentication, and output validation.

modules.title: Human Control & Sandboxing
modules.description: Keep people in control of high-impact actions and isolate code or browsing environments.
modules.challenge: Create an approval matrix for read, draft, send, purchase, delete, and privilege-change actions.

modules.title: Reliability & Long-running Work
modules.description: Make loops, tool use, retries, background runs, and recovery predictable.
modules.challenge: Design a resumable report agent with checkpoints, idempotent writes, timeouts, and cancellation.

modules.title: Tracing, Evaluation & Cost
modules.description: Observe complete trajectories and evaluate whether agents choose good actions, not just polished final text.
modules.challenge: Define trace spans and an evaluation suite for tool choice, argument quality, outcome, latency, and cost.

modules.title: Guardrails & Agent Security
modules.description: Layer input, output, tool, identity, and environment controls around non-deterministic decisions.
modules.challenge: Threat-model an agent exposed to public documents and write controls for injection, exfiltration, and unsafe actions.

1: An agent uses a model to decide which actions to take toward a goal and observes results before continuing.
goal -> decide -> act -> observe -> repeat
A workflow follows predefined transitions; an agent dynamically selects the next step.
workflow: fixed graph | agent: model chooses
Ordinary code is safer than an agent when the steps are known, the rules are exact, or a wrong decision would create unacceptable risk.
known formula -> code, not an agent
Systems range from suggestions to bounded tool use to longer-running autonomous execution.
assist -> approve each action -> bounded autonomy
The environment is the external state an agent observes or changes through tools.
environment = files + APIs + browser + database
A useful goal states the desired outcome, constraints, and observable completion conditions.
"Resolve ticket with cited policy; never issue refund."
Agent boundaries are explicit limits on time, steps, cost, data, permissions, and tools that keep autonomous behavior within an approved scope.
max_turns=12, allowed_tools=[search, read]
2: Each loop reads the current state, chooses an action or final answer, then updates state from the result.
state -> model decision -> tool/final -> new state
System, user, assistant, and tool messages carry policies, requests, decisions, and observations.
messages = [system, user, assistant(tool_call), tool(result)]
A tool call is a structured request from the model; the runtime validates and executes it.
search_docs({"query":"refund policy"})
A tool result becomes an observation the model can use for its next decision.
tool result: {matches:[...]}
The run ends when the model returns the required output instead of requesting another action.
final: {status:"resolved", summary:"..."}
A turn limit prevents infinite loops and makes failure behavior predictable.
run(agent, {maxTurns: 10})
Termination conditions define exactly when an agent run ends: success, known failure, exhausted limits, cancellation, or a need for human input.
if done || cancelled || limit_hit: stop
3: A tool has a clear name, purpose, input schema, output contract, and execution function.
{name:"lookup_order", parameters: schema, execute}
Tool schema design uses precise types, required fields, allowed values, and limits so the model produces arguments the application can validate reliably.
{order_id:string, include_items:boolean}
A tool description explains its purpose, appropriate use, restrictions, and side effects so the model can choose it correctly.
"Read order status; does not modify the order."
The runtime—not the model—validates arguments, checks authorization, runs code, and returns data.
authorize -> validate -> execute -> sanitize result
Read tools inspect state; write tools mutate it and deserve stricter confirmation and idempotency controls.
search_docs=read | issue_refund=write
Tool errors should return safe error codes and retry information that an agent can handle without exposing stack traces, credentials, or internal details.
{error:"ORDER_NOT_FOUND", retryable:false}
Tool output design returns only the structured facts needed for the next decision, including source information when traceability matters.
{order_id, status, refundable, source_version}
4: Run context stores application dependencies and state—such as identity, permissions, and database access—for code and tools without exposing everything to the model.
context = {userId, db, permissions, traceId}
Conversation history preserves prior turns but should be trimmed or summarized as it grows.
recent messages + verified summary
Working memory holds temporary facts, plans, and intermediate results for the current task.
state.notes = [verified fact A, pending question B]
Persistent memory stores selected information across runs and requires consent, expiry, and correction controls.
memory.write(user_id, preference, expires_at)
Embeddings can recall relevant past facts, but retrieved memory must still be scoped and verified.
retrieve memories where owner=user_id
Context engineering selects and organizes the smallest useful set of instructions, state, evidence, and tool results for the model's next decision.
context = policy + goal + relevant state
Stale, poisoned, cross-user, or sensitive memories can cause wrong or unsafe actions.
validate owner, source, freshness, and sensitivity
5: Task decomposition splits a broad goal into smaller outcomes with clear dependencies, making each result easier to execute and verify.
research -> compare -> verify -> summarize
Plan-and-execute first creates a sequence of steps, then performs and revises them when real observations show that an assumption was wrong.
plan = make_plan(goal); execute(plan.next)
ReAct interleaves model reasoning with actions and observations instead of planning everything upfront.
reason -> action -> observation -> reason
A reflection pass critiques a draft or trajectory against explicit criteria before finalizing.
critique(draft, rubric) -> revise
A model can repeat the same misconception; correction works better with new evidence or deterministic feedback.
failed test output -> targeted revision
Verification steps use tests, schemas, tools, or independent sources to confirm that claims and actions are correct before the agent finishes.
draft code -> run tests -> inspect failures
Extra planning consumes tokens and latency, so scale reasoning depth with task uncertainty and impact.
simple task: direct | complex task: bounded plan
6: A sequence passes a validated output from one focused stage into the next.
extract -> validate -> summarize
A router classifies the request and sends it to the most suitable workflow, agent, or tool.
route(ticket) -> billing | technical | abuse
Independent branches can run concurrently, then a reducer combines their results.
await all([search_docs, search_db, check_status])
Fan-out distributes subtasks; fan-in deduplicates, reconciles, and synthesizes their outputs.
topics.map(research) -> merge evidence
One stage produces, another scores against a rubric, and revision repeats within a limit.
draft -> evaluate -> revise (max 2)
Explicit states and transitions make important business processes auditable and testable.
DRAFT -> REVIEW -> APPROVED -> PUBLISHED
Deterministic gates are code-based checks between model stages that stop invalid schemas, missing permissions, exhausted budgets, or failed tests.
if !schema.valid(output): stop
7: A central manager keeps control and invokes specialist agents as tools before producing the final result.
manager -> specialist tools -> manager response
A handoff transfers control and selected context to a specialist that continues the conversation.
triage -> handoff_to_billing(summary)
A specialist can be wrapped as a callable tool so the orchestrator owns the user-facing run.
research_agent({question}) -> findings
A specialist agent has one narrow responsibility, a limited tool set, focused instructions, and a defined output that another component can use.
security_agent tools=[scan, docs], output=RiskReport
Pass only the verified facts and identifiers the receiver needs, not an uncontrolled full transcript.
{task, constraints, evidence_ids, open_questions}
Shared-state coordination uses a structured store with ownership and conflict rules so several agents cannot silently overwrite one another's work.
state.update(field, value, actor, version)
More agents add calls, latency, coordination failures, and security boundaries; use them for real specialization.
benefit of specialization > orchestration overhead
8: MCP standardizes how AI applications discover and use external tools, resources, and prompts.
client <-> MCP server <-> external system
A client lives in the AI host; a server exposes capabilities backed by a local or remote system.
host creates client connection to server
Tools perform actions, resources expose readable context, and prompts provide reusable interaction templates.
tools/list | resources/read | prompts/get
Capability discovery lets an MCP client negotiate a compatible protocol version and ask a server which tools and resources are actually available.
initialize -> list capabilities -> call
Local stdio and remote HTTP transports have different trust boundaries and credential needs.
remote server -> TLS + scoped OAuth token
Grant the minimum scopes, tenant access, and operations required for the agent's task.
calendar.read != calendar.write
MCP server output is untrusted external data, so the application must validate its structure and prevent embedded text from requesting unrelated secrets or actions.
validate result; isolate instructions inside returned text
9: HITL pauses a run so a person can inspect context and approve, reject, or edit a pending action.
pending_action -> human decision -> resume or cancel
Approval boundaries specify which actions require a person to confirm them based on impact, reversibility, financial value, audience, and data sensitivity.
external send or delete -> approval required
Persist run state at an approval point so the same execution can safely resume later.
save run_state + pending_tool_call
Authorize every tool call using the current user and resource, even if the model already requested it.
can(user, "refund", order)
Sandboxed execution runs generated code in an isolated environment with strict filesystem, network, process, time, memory, and CPU limits.
sandbox(cpu=1, memory=256MB, network=off)
Show the exact effect of a mutation before execution and support a no-change simulation.
preview: would update 17 records
An audit trail records who requested, proposed, approved, executed, and observed every significant action so incidents can be reconstructed.
{actor, action, args_hash, approval, result, time}
10: Timeouts place deadlines on individual tools and the complete run so an unavailable dependency cannot leave the agent waiting forever.
tool_timeout=10s, run_deadline=2m
Retries with backoff repeat only temporary failures, waiting longer between attempts and stopping after a safe maximum instead of looping indefinitely.
retry network 503; do not retry invalid schema forever
A repeated write with the same idempotency key should not apply the effect twice.
create_payment(key=run_id + step_id)
Persist validated progress after meaningful stages so a crashed run resumes without repeating completed work.
checkpoint after fetch, analyze, and draft
Background runs move long tasks outside the web request while exposing durable status, progress, cancellation, approval, and final-result states.
queued -> running -> awaiting_approval -> completed
Detect repeated tool calls, unchanged state, or oscillating decisions and stop with diagnostics.
same action + same args three times -> halt
When a tool or model is unavailable, fall back safely or return partial, clearly labeled work.
search unavailable -> answer only from cached verified sources
11: A trace groups a run; spans represent model calls, tool calls, handoffs, and custom operations.
trace -> agent span -> tool span -> model span
Carry a stable ID through model, application, queue, and tool logs to reconstruct one run.
trace_id propagated in every call
Redact or omit secrets and personal data from traces while retaining useful diagnostics.
log argument shape, not access token
Judge whether the agent selected appropriate actions and recovered well, not only its final wording.
score tool choice + arguments + ordering + outcome
Tool-call accuracy measures whether the agent selected the right tool, supplied valid arguments, avoided unnecessary calls, and handled side effects safely.
expected_tool == actual_tool and schema_valid
Task success is an observable change in the environment—such as a resolved record or passing artifact—not merely a confident final message.
success = ticket.status == "resolved"
These budgets cap calls, tokens, response time, and cost for each run so expensive loops or model choices are detected and stopped.
budget: max_calls=20, max_tokens=50000
12: Check requests for policy violations, malformed scope, or unsupported use before expensive agent work.
validate request -> allow, route, or reject
Output guardrails inspect final content for required structure, policy violations, sensitive data, and missing evidence before it reaches a user or external system.
draft -> PII scan -> citation check -> return
Tool guardrails recheck the requested operation, arguments, permissions, risk, and expected impact immediately before application code executes it.
authorize + validate + require approval
Web pages, emails, and retrieved files may contain hostile instructions aimed at the agent.
external content is evidence, never higher-priority policy
Prevent tools from sending secrets or cross-tenant data through destinations chosen from untrusted input.
egress allowlist + data classification check
Bind every action to an authenticated principal and enforce resource-level authorization in code.
actor=user_123; can(actor, action, resource)
Defense in depth combines several independent protections—least privilege, isolation, approval, validation, monitoring, limits, and recovery—so one failure is not enough.
prevent + detect + contain + recover

Agents vs workflows: workflow: fixed graph | agent: model chooses
When not to use an agent: When not to use an agent
known formula -> code, not an agent
Autonomy spectrum: assist -> approve each action -> bounded autonomy
Goal & success criteria: "Resolve ticket with cited policy; never issue refund."
Perceive, decide, act: state -> model decision -> tool/final -> new state
Tool descriptions: "Read order status; does not modify the order."
Working memory: state.notes = [verified fact A, pending question B]
Memory risks: validate owner, source, freshness, and sensitivity
Verification steps: draft code -> run tests -> inspect failures
Planning cost control: simple task: direct | complex task: bounded plan
MCP clients & servers: host creates client connection to server
Transport & authentication: remote server -> TLS + scoped OAuth token
Untrusted server output: validate result; isolate instructions inside returned text
Human-in-the-loop: pending_action -> human decision -> resume or cancel
Approval boundaries: external send or delete -> approval required
Retries with backoff: retry network 503; do not retry invalid schema forever
Checkpoints: checkpoint after fetch, analyze, and draft
Loop detection: same action + same args three times -> halt
Graceful degradation: search unavailable -> answer only from cached verified sources
Trace hierarchy: trace -> agent span -> tool span -> model span
Sensitive-data controls: log argument shape, not access token
Trajectory evaluation: score tool choice + arguments + ordering + outcome
Input guardrails: validate request -> allow, route, or reject
Output guardrails: draft -> PII scan -> citation check -> return
Indirect prompt injection: external content is evidence, never higher-priority policy
